items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-05-27
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Yeah, well you've got Pops Foster and Paul Ballgren, Monty Johnson and Eddie Conda and Louie Russell. [INTERVIEWEE] Oh, they're just playing.

ctx.x: In the Texas area? In the Texas area? No, because they, they had a different way of playing music. Mm-hmm. See, Piran, you confine yourself to what was happening here in New Orleans. Mm-hmm. And these fellas in Texas, uh, they weren't familiar with the musician from, from New Orleans, or from Louisiana, I'd say. Uh, maybe just a few, one, two a year. Mm-hmm. It's not enough to patent that. Yeah. So, that, that type of music was built on a different type of feeling.
Well, stock arrangements was stock arrangements. That's right. But, uh, when I hear a band today playing stocks from, say, 1915, every band that plays them, plays them a little different.

Don Albert made it 27, 1972. And I wanted to get into Mahogany Hall's Stomp and the way Louie holds a note on that, huh? Do you remember how Louie can hold a note? Right. You've got a good rhythm section there.
